claim: With separation and cohesion at their defaults but alignment off, the flock should not settle on a shared heading.
derivation: Expected, not derived: this is the brief's first example with separation and cohesion left on at their defaults.

Each remaining rule steers velocity toward a desired velocity set only by relative positions: toward the local centre (E4) or away from crowding (E5). Over a group these point inward and outward in roughly cancelling directions.
Their −v_i terms damp any shared motion of a group at a rate near w_c + w_s, so nothing sustains a common heading and agreement should stay well below 1.
Not guaranteed: attraction–repulsion models without explicit alignment can still align under some settings. A failure here is a finding to investigate, not a threshold to tune.
